title: Hartland Clothing Company, Main Street built in 1920
description: The Hartland Clothing Company was founded in 1915 by Anthony Baker, Arthur Dickinson, and Rex York. In 1920, they built a two-storey concrete building with a white front and a basement, which they rented to William Carr for painting cars and carriages. In 1930, the company began selling women’s clothing, hired a female sales associate, and used a truck to deliver goods door-to-door. Fred Dickinson, Arthur’s son, joined in 1935. Baker sold his share to Dickinson and York in 1938. Wilmot Dickinson (Another son of Arthur) joined after World War II. The store was expanded and updated in the 1940s. After Arthur Dickinson died in 1954 and Rex York died in 1958, Fred Dickinson became president. In 1966, the store got a new front and started selling furniture upstairs. Wilmot died in 1977, just before the store burned down in 1980.
